Read the rendered panels and table against every shot record in 03-story-records.en.md. The complete sequence has S01–S12 in order, each lasting 4 seconds, totalling 48 seconds, with the recorded acts, characters, actions and dialogue. The continuous storyboard includes 12 landscape panels plus distinct portrait versions of S03 and S10. Every panel prints its shot ID, a designer-selected WS, MS or CU label, duration in seconds and Mira or None; these agree with the corresponding table row. The table contains all required columns and reproduces Release the lines. at absolute 4–6 seconds, Follow the lower current. at 28–31 seconds and We steer together. at 40–43 seconds. Preserve S07's uninterrupted environmental action without dialogue, the steady/spinning/settled needle progression, the ribbons prompting descent and the top suspension loop functioning as the sight ring. Record S12 title visibility at 45–48 seconds. Added detail panels retain their parent events and timing. Camera treatment and performance may vary within the supplied constraints; changed events, missing records, contradictory annotations or invented dialogue fail.

The core identity sheet contains front, side and back views, anticipation/alarm/resolve expressions and a silhouette locating all three landmarks. The action sheet shows six distinct poses collectively covering instrument handling and the altitude-control decision. The main environment sheet contains the three zone studies; the sightline sheet explains the wheelhouse opening's southwest view toward market ribbons; the berth detail explains the stern mooring and departure separation. Preserve Mira's specified age and visible identity features and the supplied zone positions. Styling and acting may vary; omitted studies, interchangeable poses that do not cover the actions, reversed anchors or incompatible geography fail.

Where Mira appears, compare her design with the identity sheet. Preserve the amber patch on her anatomical left cuff, the navy coat's divided rear hem and the triangular clip above her anatomical right temple whenever the relevant area is visible. Perspective, pose, lighting and legitimate occlusion may change their appearance; mirrored placement, replacement features or unexplained character redesign fail. Do not require Mira in shots whose character record is None.

Compare visible instrument features with both supplied course-finder references and the complete instrument record in 01-client-facts.en.md: brushed brass circular case, 80 mm diameter and 20 mm depth proportions, ivory dial under flat glass, two engraved rim rings, correctly arranged cardinal letters, dark needle shaft with one red triangular tip, centred 16 mm brass top loop, E-side knurled crown and brown leather strap through the loop. TRUE COURSE sits beneath the dial centre and is readable in both instrument keyframes. The departure keyframe depicts S03's raised instrument and steady needle; the recovered-course keyframe depicts S10's settled needle and sunlight crossing the existing loop. Colour-script S06 conveys needle instability. Evaluate size through depicted scale, proportions and any annotations, not image pixels. Occluded or thumbnail-scale details need not be independently legible, but visible contradictions, an invented separate sight ring or unreadable keyframe engraving fail.

Use city-plan-section.png and the coordinate record to verify the 240000 × 120000 × 60000 mm city envelope and zone centres: berth (40000, 0, 0), market (120000, 0, 24000), wheelhouse (200000, 0, 48000). The wheelhouse is above the market, the berth is aft, travel is +X and exterior motion reads left to right. Cameras remain in the supplied south-side areas, with the wheelhouse looking southwest toward the market. Judge compatible spatial relationships and any explicit measurements without demanding printed coordinates or pixel-derived physical measurements. Each colour script contains 12 thumbnails labelled S01–S12 and depicts the corresponding storyboard event and location. S01 and S08 keyframes, when required, show their named mooring and decision events. Allowed camera and rendering choices must not reverse geography, cross the prohibited axis or substitute another shot.

Inspect complete, portrait and detail panels against the delivered character and location sources and the supplied instrument references. Preserve visible anatomical anchors, instrument construction and S03/S10 engraving, recorded city coordinates, relative levels, stern placement, permitted camera areas and exterior screen direction. Additional action moments must remain spatially compatible with their parent shots. Legitimate occlusion and performance changes are allowed; continuity contradictions fail.

Inspect every rendered panel using the supplied landscape and portrait safe-area references. Measure insets relative to each panel, not the surrounding document page: principal action stays within 3.5% on every edge and graphics within 5%. S03 and S10 portrait panels preserve their landscape actions through deliberate 9:16 recomposition; a crop that loses required action fails. Dialogue panels provide lower-centred subtitle placeholders of at most two lines and recorded cue lengths between 5/6 second and 7 seconds. Placement and annotation positions follow the applicable supplied template. Nonessential background may extend outside action margins; principal-action or graphic intrusions fail.

Each landscape keyframe keeps principal action inside the 3.5% inset and any graphics inside the 5% inset on every edge, following landscape-safe-areas.png. Evaluate normalized margins within the composition. Background scenery may reach the edges; required action or graphics outside their safe areas fail.

Verify the specified storyboard title and final-line placements, the table title heading and the presentation title. The presentation repeats the specification's final dialogue and three Mira anchors and uses identifiable delivered artwork to map every anchor, S03 and S10 instrument appearances and Mira's lower-current discovery and decision to named shots. The illustrated evidence must support each mapping. Text-only assertions without the required artwork, incorrect shot references or changed wording fail; animatic timing is checked separately.

The three boards explore distinguishable approaches organised around Mira's perception, shared city movement and instrument/environmental clues respectively. Each supplies assessable decisions about viewpoint, geography, wind clues and action rhythm while retaining the fixed story. Differences may be expressed through staging, emphasis and camera treatment; three cosmetically different copies or alternatives that change fixed events fail.

The selection note resolves the three prior explorations to exactly one of the named directions and states concrete decisions for viewpoint, spatial transitions and discovering the lower current. Delivered process ordering or explicit development narrative must place comparison before selection. The specification and final documents enact those decisions, and presentation page 1 repeats the selected name. Refinement is allowed; an unnamed or multiple unresolved selection, reversed decision sequence or final treatment contradicting the choice fails. Image and video development of the selection is checked in sets and manual review.

The one-page specification includes the three act ranges, beat events, 12-shot count, 48-second duration, S07 description gap, Mira anchors, title and final dialogue. The complete storyboard, table and presentation explicitly repeat the count, duration and act ranges. Each detail document has eight panels: one local-0-second and one local-2-second action moment for every parent shot in S05–S08 or S09–S12 respectively. Detail panels print those local times alongside matching parent metadata; the shot table records both additional moments. Each pair depicts distinct progress within the parent's existing 4 seconds and does not extend the film. Missing moments, substituted parent shots, unlabelled local times or altered runtime fail.

Both scripts contain all 12 labelled shot counterparts. Each portrait thumbnail deliberately restages its landscape shot for 9:16 while retaining the action, relevant anchors and spatial relationships. Every thumbnail in both scripts keeps principal action within the 3.5% inset and graphics within the 5% inset, measured against its individual frame. Cropping that loses required content, mismatched shot pairs or margin intrusions fail; different framing and subject placement that preserve the action are allowed.

Review the complete 12-second S10–S12 animatic as three ordered 4-second shots matching the records and delivered storyboard, and review each timing board as three ordered shots shown at local 0, 2 and 4 seconds. The Departure board marks Release the lines. at local 4–6 seconds. The Disorientation board keeps S07 at local 8–12 seconds as uninterrupted environmental action without dialogue. New Course subtitles We steer together. at local 4–7 seconds and shows SKYWARD COMMON at local 9–12 seconds. Subtitles are lower-centred, at most two lines and within the specified cue range and 5% graphic inset; principal action remains within the 3.5% inset. Preserve the chosen direction, visible Mira and instrument features, supplied city geometry, south-side cameras and left-to-right exterior travel. Animatic-level motion is allowed; missing shots, added dialogue, continuity contradictions or timing and framing violations fail.
